parsed.explanation: Combined regime is state-enforced: airport appearance-versus-passport screening with genital X-ray, mockery, entry refusal and confiscation documented from 2016 to 2025; gender nonconformity is criminal with up to one year's imprisonment under Article 412(2) and broader prior enforcement; visitors were imprisoned, held in an effeminate-detainee cell, head-shaved, had hormones discarded, fined and deported. Detention mistreatment including beatings and forced rectal examinations is documented. No registration, openly operating organisation, discrimination protection or effective remedy is documented. Rule-of-law efficiency enforces the hostile rules.

entry_documents.exposure: Airport screening compares appearance to passport sex; 2025 visitors were X-rayed for genital anatomy, mocked, refused entry and had passports confiscated. Similar refusals documented across a decade at two main gateways.
entry_documents.protection: Not documented. No rule accepting a passport marker matching presentation is documented.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch triggers detention, investigation, possible criminal exposure and deportation before any local remedy can operate.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Visitors held for hours or months, imprisoned for one year, held nearly three weeks in an effeminate-detainee cell, head-shaved and hormone pills discarded. Beatings and forced rectal examinations described as torture in detention.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented. No independent custody placement, medical-continuity or consular remedy is shown to work.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry or street encounter becomes arrest, presentation prosecution, sex-segregated/effeminate-cell custody, then deportation rather than release.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Article 412(2) punishes a man disguising as a woman to enter a women-only space with up to one year's imprisonment and a 10,000-dirham fine. Prior enforcement reached mixed-gender malls and public places based on appearance.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Not documented. Private hospitality cannot override the federal offence or the local public-morals offence applied alongside it.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal and emirate-level morals enforcement operate together; using a women-only facility can itself trigger the criminal exposure.

care_services.exposure: Hormone pills were discarded during detention. A trans foreigner remained detained from September 2022 to at least April 2023 after refusing a toxicology test; outcome unresolved. Emergency or routine care access for visitors is not documented.
care_services.protection: Not documented. No visitor care shield, medication-continuity protection or independent hospital complaint process is documented.
care_services.interaction: Detention interrupts medication and treatment; hospital discovery creates a further outing and enforcement risk.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Gender nonconformity is expressly criminalised; officials have said there is no room for homosexual and queer acts. Police campaigns, raids, venue closure, censorship and internet blocking reinforce state hostility.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Not documented. Organisations cannot register and no openly operating support structure exists.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat-framing legitimises border screening, street stops, raids and custodial abuse; courts and agencies provide no documented counterweight.

minors_guardians.exposure: No child-specific trans protection is documented. A trans minor would face the same entry screening, presentation offence and custody exposure as an adult.
minors_guardians.protection: Not documented. Article 409(5) guardian-complaint structure concerns same-sex-conduct prosecutions, not visitors' gender presentation, and gives no protective remedy here.
minors_guardians.interaction: A parent or guardian cannot localise or waive federal entry, facility or detention rules for a travelling minor.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Police have raided gatherings, run campaigns targeting transsexuals and masculine-presenting women, arrested people solely for looking feminine, and deported foreign residents for clothing. Custodial beatings and torture are documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Not documented. No effective prosecution of attackers, police accountability or victim-protection process is shown.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Calling police, as in the 2013 nightclub case, led to the visitors' own prolonged detention, fine and deportation.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No legal gender recognition, anti-discrimination protection, registered organisations or functioning complaint route is documented. Frequency cannot be quantified and enforcement variation between emirates is unknown.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Not documented. One tourist's public-indecency charges were dropped after head-of-government intervention, but no trans-specific remedy is documented.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Unknown aggregate frequency does not negate the documented repeated pattern; absence of remedy makes each exposure operative.

anchor_checks.comparison: Very similar: street and entry targeting for presentation, repeated visitor convictions, months to a year of imprisonment, sex-segregated custody abuse and courts applying the rule. This dossier adds engineered airport genital screening, keeping it at the severe-risk level.

Lower risk than this case: that anchor has raids, detention and custody harassment but less documented sustained airport screening, one-year visitor sentences and detention-related torture. The combined universal entry exposure and criminal offence place this below 0.25.

Higher risk than this case: that anchor has an unremedied facility exclusion but no criminal presentation offence, airport genital screening, repeated imprisonment or torture. Those additional state actions move this materially below 0.35.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller encounters one hostile system across stages: passport/appearance screening forces outing at the border, gender presentation is criminalised, police enforce it in public and facilities, custody is sex-segregated with documented abuse and medication interruption, and deportation follows. Same-sex-conduct provisions are secondary and constrained by the complainant rule, but are unnecessary to the rating because trans-specific law and enforcement already dominate. No documented protection interrupts the sequence.
